hero.lead: Freelance Unity developer specialised in gameplay, systems and networking. I turn a design intention into solid, readable mechanics that feel great to play.
projects.title: What I've built.
projects.lead: Networking, spells, rhythm, combat systems. For each project: what I actually did.
p.discosmos.desc: Implementation of the entire network layer and the character spell system of a multiplayer game built in Unity.
p.discosmos.tagline: A multiplayer game where networking and spells are the heart of the gameplay.
p.discosmos.ctx: Discosmos is a multiplayer game built in Unity with Photon. I handled the whole networking system as well as the character spell system: two building blocks that must stay perfectly consistent so every player gets a fair, readable match.
p.discosmos.c1: Network architecture: connection, rooms, player management and game-state synchronisation with Photon.
p.discosmos.c2: Spell system: spell definition, casting and applying effects to characters.
p.discosmos.c3: Multiplayer consistency: spells are triggered and replicated over the network so every player sees the same match.
p.discosmos.c4: Extensible code: structured so the team can add spells without touching the network layer.
p.beat-strike.desc: Creation of the rhythm-pattern authoring tool and of the gameplay loop that drives combat, defence and progression.
p.beat-strike.tagline: An action game where every strike is played on the beat.
p.beat-strike.ctx: In Beat Strike the level scrolls, enemies show up and the player chains tempo-synced interactions to attack and defend. I built the rhythm tool and the main gameplay loop.
p.beat-strike.c1: Rhythm tool in the Unity editor: a pattern editor to compose interaction sequences, usable by designers without touching code.
p.beat-strike.c2: Patterns per BPM: a library of attack and defence patterns, picked according to the level's tempo.
p.beat-strike.c3: Gameplay loop: level chunk sequencing, attack and defence phases, interaction spawning and combat triggering.
p.beat-strike.c4: Performance: object pooling for interactions to avoid allocations during play.
p.heroes-dawn.desc: Mobile 3D fantasy RPG: turn-based combat with an active timeline, HQ management and life-sim / MMORPG mechanics.
p.heroes-dawn.tagline: A mobile RPG where every turn is read on a timeline.
p.heroes-dawn.ctx: Heroes Dawn is a 3D fantasy RPG designed for mobile, set in the Apex Universe, the shared universe of Studio N29's projects. It combines turn-based combat on an active timeline with HQ management and mechanics inspired by life sims and MMORPGs.
p.heroes-dawn.c1: Turn-based combat with an active timeline that makes the action order readable and strategic.
p.heroes-dawn.c2: HQ management: rooms, expeditions, recruitment and squad progression, designed for mobile.
p.heroes-dawn.c3: Production documentation: GDD, game-design specs, art direction, UI flows and roadmap laid out before writing code.
p.heroes-dawn.c4: Coherent universe: the Apex Universe, shared across Studio N29 projects.
p.delight.desc: A Rubika group project being migrated to Unity 6: upgrading the project, its plugins and rendering.
p.delight.tagline: Bringing a game project back to life on Unity 6.
p.delight.ctx: Delight is a game project made in a group at Rubika. We are currently working on opening and running it on Unity 6, which means revisiting the project in depth.
p.delight.c1: Version upgrade to Unity 6: compile errors, deprecated APIs and package updates.
p.delight.c2: Plugins: replacing or removing plugins that became incompatible.
p.delight.c3: Rendering: adapting the render pipeline and post-processing profiles.
p.delight.c4: Stabilisation: checking scenes, levels and interactions after the migration.
p.project-x.desc: A project in development, under a non-disclosure agreement. Details will be published once the NDA is lifted.
p.project-x.tagline: A project in progress, under a non-disclosure agreement.
p.project-x.notice: This project is covered by a non-disclosure agreement. I can't share visuals, client names or precise technical details.
p.project-x.ctx: I contribute to the development of a Unity project built by a team. What I can say: it is in production and I work on it as a Unity developer.
p.project-x.c1: Feature development in Unity and C#, within a team.
p.project-x.c2: Strict confidentiality: no project content is published here.
p.project-x.c3: Private discussion possible: I can say more as part of a mission discussion.

about.title: Gameplay developer, trained at Rubika.
about.p1: I'm a Unity developer specialised in gameplay programming, systems and networking. I studied at Rubika (Supinfogame) in the Programming Bachelor, and I now work as a freelancer under the STUDIO N29 banner.
about.p2: I like mechanics that feel good in the hands: readable combat, a spell that responds at the right moment, networking you never notice. My experience also gave me full-stack web, LLM / AI and prompt-engineering skills.
about.p3: I fit into a team quickly, communicate clearly and like shipping code that others can pick up.
skills.title: What I can take on.
skills.1.d: Game mechanics, combat, spells and abilities, game loop, controls and game feel.
skills.2.d: Network architecture, state synchronisation, replicated actions and consistency between players.
skills.3.d: Unity tools for designers: pattern editors, custom inspectors, data-driven workflows.
skills.4.d: Managers, pooling, serialisation and data loading: clean code that scales.
skills.5.d: Back-end APIs, graph databases, LLM integration and prompt engineering.
skills.6.d: Git, cloud, 3D (Blender, Unreal) and collaboration with art and design teams.
journey.title: Where I come from.
journey.1.d: Built an AI-based back-end API on graph databases, and a narrative game in Unity that uses this API.
journey.2.d: Showcase website for used vehicles with an admin interface, and setup of the digital tools (cloud, invoicing, stock).
journey.3.d: Hardware and software maintenance, and a consumables tracking app based on QR-code scanning.
journey.4.d: Video game programming studies: gameplay, systems and networking.
